references.text: The preceding verse, which is part of the same parable about a father who gives good gifts – where it asks whether a father would give a snake instead of a fish.
Matthew's parallel text to Luke 11:11-12, where Jesus uses similar examples (bread/stone, fish/snake) to illustrate that a father gives good gifts to his children.
The conclusion of the parable: If earthly fathers know how to give good gifts, how much more will the heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.
Matthew's parallel to the conclusion in Luke 11:13 – that the heavenly Father gives good gifts to those who ask him.
James emphasizes that every good gift and every perfect gift comes from above, from the Father of lights – the same theme of God's goodness in giving gifts.
Jesus mentions scorpions in connection with the power he gives his disciples – to tread on snakes and scorpions. The scorpion motif links the verses together.
